item.title: Re: The 7th Panzer Divison
item.content:encoded:
1) Thousands of tanks worldwide is a bit overkill. An SCP shouldn't be that powerful without a was to stop it ahead of time. Either provide a way to stop it or drop it. Also, you need to decide if the ghosts are just ghosts or have actual firepower.

2) While the basic concept shows some promise, you need to build on it a little. Top FIve Quickies:
a) How did they escape back? Did they find a hole, make a deal, or just time out?
b) How did they find out that they could control the ghost tanks?
c) If you are building on the "deserted soldier" concept, why do they keep surrendering so quickly?
d) How did they manage to hide from modern sensory equipment?
e) What happens if they encounter a group of modern neo-Nazis?

3) Also, wouldn't Obskuracorp want an update on their radio?

Like I said: Good concept, just needs some filling in….

item.title: Re: Exli Apomus (EA)
item.content:encoded:
(Can't give greenlights)

Ultimately, the main challenge here is going to be rewriting your virus/parasite to stand out more. The idea of a rampant, incurable, killer virus is already pretty well trod ground in all forms of media. Not to mention, there's already many different infectious virus-like SCPs with many different anomalous effects.

+ Here's some crit
- Begone crit

The pathogen, discovered in lake Vostok, under the ancient Antarctica ice sheets, is unknown to man, is resistant to all antibodies, and is incurable by any means possible (including anomalous).

Apart from being incurable by both conventional and anomalous means, I just don't see how this particular virus is going to set itself apart. Perhaps giving the virus' victims some kind of anomalous property would be a decent place to start. Or, perhaps the virus spreads itself in some kind of anomalous fashion.

After the downfall of the urinary system, it attacks the immune system. It's main target is macrophages and B cells. Once the B cells fall to a critically low amount, it starts another attack on the immune system against the macrophages. They "bundle up" and start overwhelming the macrophages with such intense force that the guard cell just explodes. After the main targets are down, it feeds away at smaller cells, which help them grow in size. The parasites will then feast on blood rapidly, and cause mass blood clots, and stop blood flow almost entirely.

Even if its effects are somewhat gruesome and out of the ordinary, I don't quite see this virus as being anomalous enough. When it comes to strange and somewhat supernatural infections, there's a wide variety of choices. Focusing less on the realistic ways the virus infects the body and more on making the virus unique in the foundation universe will help make this concept successful.

Also, having a narrative is a pretty crucial role when it comes to giving your article legs to stand on. How was the virus discovered? How has the foundation struggled in containing it? Is there a hint that the virus was created by a known entity/GoI? These are just a few stories you can tell throughout the article.

item.title: Survey, Capture, Pursue
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Page Layout (Optional): The Containment Procedure is crossed out.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself are two books that are quantum entangled in the future. These books update as they are being written in the future. One of these books is a log of scientists trying to experiment with quantum entangling and details every single book that was entangled to the future and where to get them. This book gets taken, and the SCP Foundation has to find out who stole it using evidence and the other book, which was entangled in time by someone in the future warning them that they have to stop the thief from taking the book because society in the future will fall apart under one man's power.

Central Narrative: The central narrative is from the SCP Foundation's perspective, tracking down an object that was taken from the inside and trying to find who did it before they escape. Basically a reverse heist that explores some of the Foundation's security protocols.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Lots of twists and turns, a more story driven SCP that deals with slowly uncovering how someone stole the SCP as the Foundation tries to catch them before they escape.

item.title: Re: Hikikomori
item.content:encoded:
A hikikomori ends up as a SCP entity by means of apparent suicide, becoming capable of entering reality from other people's dreams.

First thing I will say is that I think using suicide and self harm without substantive reasons why is a bad look, and is a lazy way to show escalation. Yes, hikikomori are known to be susceptible… but self harm is not a useful part of a story that isn't addressing it in some substantive way. If you're mentioning it because "it fits" or to make it seem edgy, drop it.

capable of entering reality from other people's dreams

What does this mean? Like Freddy Krueger? Or manifesting themselves through dreams from somewhere outside our universe/reality?

Turns out that the SCP Foundation is protecting the waking reality itself by keeping that very secret.

How would this be protecting the world? What makes our world less real than someone who originated within our world and became an entity?

  • Also… like these are real people, are you sure you want to exploit the people who live their lives this way for a spooky story?
  • What about this anomaly has anything to do with self-imposed isolation? It doesn't feel connected to anything about the anomaly itself. Just someone who was ostracized from society, kills themselves, and then becomes Freddy Kruger (without the horror).

What I mean by this… is you're painting a picture using Corbenic and Insurgency… but not telling me anything about the characters. Also important to note that Corbenic isn't the organization…

Additionally, consider this: if COrbenic exists in the in-universe SCP-5000 does, then that's a new rash of humanity going to the next life once the Foundation kills everyone… as multiple alt reality Earths have arrived in Corbenic (that's where the triple moons came from) meaning Corbenic is not limited to one continua.

item.title: Worldwarden
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fantasy

Elevator Pitch:

  • Appears as a deer or other local horned mammal trapped in a tree, fence, etc.
  • Often partially consumed or decomposing but the head typically remains lifelike
  • Individuals who come across it develop aggression towards whatever development is threatening the area and causing the SCP to manifest. They gain mild supernatural strength and endurance, as well as enhanced senses and become distressed if they are kept from accomplishing damage to the development
  • Those exposed retain an increased sense of connection with wilderness, but no powers or anger
  • The deer becomes fully skeletonized and loses anomalous properties if the ecosystem is damaged beyond repair or if the "appointee" is successful in neutralizing the development. Plants will rapidly cover the site of the development

Central Narrative:
*The world is fighting back against human and anomalous incursion but offers the chance for redemption to those lucky enough to receive its blessing
*The foundation can use this phenomenon to its benefit, but only if they tread carefully
*At first it's a threat to be neutralized, but through addenda, we learn that the foundation can exploit this for MTF operatives in wilderness scenarios.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Incident log about a disastrous breach caused during the development of a new site at the hands of one of their own who came into contact with this SCP

Additional Notes:

item.title: My first SCP; The Corn Monkeys
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): SCP Format

Elevator Pitch:
A Race of monkey like creatures that:
*live in a corn field in southern Wisconsin that shows anomalous properties
*have extremely long top teeth and claws
*can use teeth and claws to extract the spine from a live human in seconds
*uses the spine to craft a makeshift tail to be used to attract a mate
*can not leave the cornfield without dying within minutes
*has i diet consisting of only corn grown in that field and human blood
*will die violently if fed anything else
*help to exponentially increase the yield of the crop grown in the field
*can mimic the crying and screams of a victims children to lure in to the field to be killed

Central Narrative:
Scp-xxxx are hairless monkey "like" creatures with large bulbous eyes and have elongated limbs. The creatures teeth and claws are also dis-proportionally elongated, with only the top portion of teeth being elongated in this way. Their spines are curved and distort wildly and they hunch over when on all four limbs. However, the spine can violently and grotesquely be straightened when threatened and standing in the up right position. Due to this violent transformation the spine is always exposed, being ripped through the skin during transformation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Scp-xxxx also posses the ability to mimic the sound of a lost child, crying and screaming for help. This has a psychological effect on most victims with children of their own as the cry's can mimic the victims offspring. It furthermore has a some what hypnotic effect on the victim, filling them with a misplaced sense of bravery and willingness to do what ever it takes to save the "lost child".

Additional Notes: I am looking for critiques and feedback on my writing. i am also seeking greenlight and any help building off this concept

item.title: Re: The 7th Panzer Division - seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Alright, so I just made some revisions to this thing and tried to make some improvements to the central narrative part of this thing.

Central narrative
Central narrative

They go into hiding in a forest after abandoning the nazi cause and uses their anomalous capability, guns, utilities, etc, to survive in the wilderness and avoid capture. As time goes on, dissidence begins to grow in each of them against the former regime they served.

During a containment breach at a nearby facility, a massive sinkhole is formed taking the tank along with her crew with it to the bottom. They survive the fall but find themselves in a world similar to our own, a damp, dark, cold world lacking any source of light. As the group ventures throughout this “underworld,” they discover that it’s populated entirely by dark, shadowy beings that bear a disfigured, grainy, slender silhouette of a human. Worst yet is that they seem to be on the hunt for the tank crew.

Looking for a way out and forced to survive in this new world against these creatures, the tank crew utilize what limited ammunition and supply they have left on them to ensure the safety of their survival. Eventually, the tank that they utilized began to slowly change, with deep scratch marks being discovered both inside and outside the tank. The tank crew were ready to abandon the tank thinking that it was beginning to wear down until the radio man discovered that using the radio at a certain frequency would spawn a massive WWII era german tank army filled with mighty caliber guns capable of toppling the deadliest war machines ever built, and armour that were incapable of penetration.

It would only be decades later when the group would return to our world with their hand in the air, surrounded by SCP agents during an investigation into the sinkhole. When reappearing from the underworld, the tank crew would utilize their tank army as a show of defiance against their new captors, only to realize that the former tank army that was made of the toughest armour had become a hazy, transparent division. Objects would come and go through the ghost tanks, causing little harm as the screams of horrors by soldiers being gunned down and mutilated would play as they rolled past, deafening the roaring engines of the tanks.

The tank crew would eventually be captured and held in captivity by SCP researchers putting an end to their escape. Days later, ghosts of tanks would appear throughout Europe and North Africa, firing upon civilian homes, shopping centres, gas stations and random buildings leaving destruction and tens to hundreds of casualties with zero traces of the ghosts left. An interview conducted on the tank crew would show similarities in both their journey in the underworld and the aforementioned incident in terms of behaviour, actions and locations.

It's a lot to take in but it's my attempt at improving it, giving it some kind of story to it and just being my first SCP in general

Criticisms and critiques would be appreciated

item.title: Re: Draft 'GHOSTEATER', ver. 1
item.content:encoded:
Giving crit cuz I was sniped on the idea forums

howdy, I'm yellow, and ima be dropping a critique today.

lbl
– hide block

The body was found at 4:13pm on a Sunday.

This is definitely a trope, and I love that trope, but it does make readers roll their eyes sometimes. Be wary.

If you could even call it that.

A body, I mean.

Making these all into separate lines feels like it is trying to add emphasis where it really isn't needed. I understand the intro with the whole "hook in" part, but making these two lines doesn't feel terribly necessary.

When the first unwitting civilian stumbled upon it, it was still a steaming pile of viscera rendered inside-out by some unknown force, fragmented polygons of ivory bone jutting through the pulped remains of flesh and muscle, sinew and organs.

This is all one sentence. This could use breaking up at least into two sentences.

Remarkably, the extremities were intact: hands and wrists, shins and feet, the neck and head.

This is a long list giving emphasis, yes, but the way it is formatted really irks with me. Commas are present at some points yet aren't?

By the time I arrived, the blood had coagulated like carmine veins in the cracks of the flagstones. A dank and metallic smell lingered about the scene my cohorts had established with their cheery yellow markers.
We were quick to establish ground here ahead of civilian police. This was far beyond their jurisdiction.

I'm liking this part, but this all could be one paragraph.

My senior officer - Officer Dalton - gave me the details, and we discussed the evidence.

You could honestly state My senior officer Dalton and have the same feel here.

Officer Dalton hums and haws a bit. “I suppose.”

hums and haws feels weird here, but I suppose it works. I will note that using "they" would be a lot less clunky, and make the sentence flow better.

“None that we could find. What’s your ChemAnalysis say?”

Consider Chem-Analysis

The air was damp, so it lingered, and even an unmodified person could easily tell.

What does "unmodified" mean in this context? Consider a different word usage.

“Nothing. No explosive residue or anything. May I -?” I gesture to the remains.

When it comes to cut-offs, typically, the paragraph ends there. Also, a cut off doesn't work the best here. Consider the following:

“Nothing. No explosive residue or anything." I gesture my body to the remains. "May I?"

I make my way over, stepping around various items of gore and little yellow placards.

what does "various items of gore" refer to? The grammar here needs re-wording.

A quick scan with my eyepiece maps the blood-spattered albeit intact face to an online repository of personnel records - and finds a match.

This sentence pacing goes by very fast, and needs a comma.

“Interesting they left all of the uh, identifying components intact,” I say aloud to nobody in particular. “We got a matching face ID, prolly fingerprints too if we took’em.”

Very strange use of dialogue here, feels more fake, or a thought, over a real person speaking to themself. When people speak to themselves, they typically tend to be more realistic with themself, like speaking to another, but on a deeper level.

“Your job is literally full-time Zombie.”

Grammar is clunky here.

The on-call medic hovers about like a nervous fly, until I wave him off.

happens way to fast, needs better pacing. Break into two sentences is my best advice.

The brain had already begun to decay and so, much like a VCR tape degraded through magnetic interference, the images began to decay with it.

Slow down pacing here, this is on the verge of being a run-on sentence.

Despite my own thoughts being in-tact I could feel the ghost of the other mind’s presence alongside my own, unaware of its death and guiding the body through the busy street as it could remember doing.

Problems with this sentence:

  • in-tact should be intact
  • run on sentence
  • fast paced sentence, needs more commas

As I mused this the world shifted around me, twisting in on itself and re-orientating as the dimly-lit interior of a dated café.

These should be two separate sentences, one for each concept in the sentence.

The body looks up, and sat in front of us is an attractive albeit ordinary-looking woman

You use the term "albeit" a lot, and whenever you use that word, you use a double comma. Example:

He was strong, albeit lanky and undertoned.

“I wanted to discuss a deal,” She says, the cadence of her voice song-like and airy. “We are aware of your expertise, Mr. Rutkowski, and we believe that there may be mutual benefits to be found.”

I don't like this part. It feels fake and forced, a rather underwhelming interpretation of professionalism.

Quickly noting this because I don't want to be noting this throughout the entirety of the lbl. The dialogue pacing feels incredibly forced, and I never felt immersed in the characters. It feels as though I am simply learning the information on its own, and not hearing two distinct and real characters conversing with each other. I recommend going back and redoing the dialogue, and consider reading it aloud, as that helps catch and distinctify forced dialogue. Dialogue is the focal point of this article to me, but as of now, it is somewhat underwhelming, and could use reworking.

“We are just…mmm, well informed.”

"mmm" is a strange onamonapia

“ - forget it. I can’t - I can’t do this not knowing what’s gonna happen to me. You could be lying. I won’t.”

The grammar here is poor, but that is acceptable seeing the current predicament. However, I will not that this is paced incredibly strangely for a situation like this. I strongly urge you to make them speak much more slower then normal, as if they are trying to put together thoughts.

The gentle clack-clack-clack of footsteps was almost palpable, down the alley.

Remove comma, yet another onamonapia, which feels off for an article like this.

No longer doing line by line beyond this point, I felt disinterest beyond here, and will read to finish and give overall concept review.

concept/overall
– hide block
Concept

My senior officer - Officer Dalton - gave me the details, and we discussed the evidence.

This part irks with me a lot. An entire bit of dialogue has been replaced with a single line, when dialogue could be used here to help build up the world surrounding this tale. I recommend changing this to dialogue, and giving more depth to the conversation beyond the following three lines. The discussion of evidence could help delve deeper into the story itself.

It must’ve rained at some point during his trip.

I don't wish to break this to you, but rain is the one thing that breaks immersion the most. When it rains onto people, they typically break any "immersion" they have in what they are doing, and tend to note the rain. It's a natural biological response from the body. Even when in crisis, people are able to distinguish different liquids splashing onto their bodies. Look it up, it's a real thing. In any case, the part about being wet is somewhat unnecessary, so the best way to explain this would to be omitting the concept as a whole.

Overall

I would like to begin by noting that I specifically did not read through the idea pitch in the forums (partially because I did not have the time to). I would have gone back and read it, but I believe that your article should be able to convey the same experience to me without having to read anything beyond it. For this reason, I am giving critique based without the knowledge of events.

Right away, I want to note on something that irked me a lot when reading; The ending.

The last thing I remember is the medic’s heavy hand on my shoulder, and his voice, barely audible.

This felt so… underwhelming? I felt like the ending would have dragged on at least a bit more, but I felt dissatisfied when finishing this. The entirety of the article was fairly okay, but the ending disappointed me when reading through. I wished for it to be a bit more "huzzah", more concluding then "the last thing I remembered." I suggest adding a line similar to the common trope of "then everything went black." etc. It works very well in these situations, adding a sort of "cliffhanger" which provides a nice concluding ending.

Concept-wise, there were points where I was confused, but I can do very little to help with the concept. Line by line is my strength. However, I will note that it could be reworded a lot to help readers understand what you are saying better. An example of this would be your extreme use of metaphor. It was nice, but it could be cut down upon quite a hefty amount.

However, as an article, the core concept was fairly decent. Very nice concept with a easy to follow working.

format tingz
– hide block

If you could even call it that.
A body, I mean.

Break up by one more line. This happens a lot, but for both reader convenience and consistency, break all paragraphs up by two lines:

like

this

INITIALISING NECRO-NEURAL INTERROGATION

INTENTIONS FOUND TO BE IN VIOLATION OF THE 2027 NEUROTRANSMISSION ACT WILL BE MET WITH DISCIPLINARY ACTIONS AS DESCRIBED THEREIN

… INITIALISATION COMPLETE

I don't particularly like how these are all separate, especially since nothing happens in between these events. I suggest putting things in between over making it into one box, as one box will make this clunky, and the wording adds character.

Hmm. A majority of the paragraph breaks in this article feel unjustified, adding emphasis to specific points and dividing up reader concepts. I suggest making this more paragraph-based, as having a separate line this many times really messes with the reader POV.

“We are just…mmm, well informed.”

do this instead (for …)

“We are just… mmm, well informed.”

“ - forget it. I can’t - I can’t do this not knowing what’s gonna happen to me. You could be lying. I won’t.”

change hyphens

“-forget it. I can’t- I can’t do this not knowing what’s gonna happen to me. You could be lying. I won’t.”


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Drafts Critique
Forum thread: Draft 'GHOSTEATER', ver. 1

The core idea here is definitely viable. Classic vanilla killer monsters are hard to pull off, but the anomaly is a good one to carry something like that. Ditch the targeting of people who know about it and the sound-trigger thing; this thing only needs the one party trick. It's a solid one.

I'm just going to do a rough breakdown here, if you take this to the forums for an overhaul and second try (and you should) PM me and I'll do a more in-depth one. I'm being a little blunt here because I think this is a strong idea but it will only work with a total overhaul.

The surface problems are tone breaks and bad formatting - scare italics in the Containment procedures, overdramatic statements of how dangerous it is, directly addressing the reader, hard-to-read paragraph organization… lots of little things that draft critique can help you address.

More than that though, you're totally missing the mark on what makes this thing a good monster, and how to present it. There's a lot here telling us we should be afraid of this thing, and not nearly enough showing us any of it. Tied into that, you also show your cards way, way too early, especially with regard to the strongest parts of this.

For instance, Don't beat us over the head with everything that qualifies as a pipe immediately in the containment procedures. Keep it subtle, just say it has to be kept x meters from tube-like structures or objects, and describe how it moves between pipes and manipulates the flow of things through them. And then let it click into place when the containment team points a gun at it. You can do the same with containment breaches demonstrating the endless series of things which can be considered tubes. There's potential for this thing to be scary as hell, it just needs to be used right.

I love this. I'm a sucker for the more psychological horrors, like SCP-3001, the ones that use emotion to fuck with you. It's amazing, and it's honestly chilling in a nice way.

As a reader, I'd personally want Blue to be right: that the entire anomaly is just an anomalous divider between the groups. But in reality, it's like Model Red, because otherwise…

But you can't know. No one does. And if Ehwez tries to figure it out, it could spell completely disaster.

The line that best sums this up is this:

We could be sitting on a landmine, or on a cushion, and either way it would really be a poor idea to get up right now.

My only complaint is the Model Blue and Model Red coloring in the object class is a bit unfriendly (the rest of the colored text has context). I'd add a small footnote to the Object Class, but that's it.

Good job!

item.title: Re: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"
item.content:encoded:
I've thought about this several times, and I could never be loyal to the SCP Foundation as it stands in-universe. The Foundation commits human rights violations without a second thought at every turn, even when completely unnecessary, and their fundamental approach to the anomalous is flawed. For every -EX, there are a dozen "unexplained" anomalies which are totally understood by the Foundation's understanding of science and could easily be added to current sciences. Memetics, the multiverse, and SCP-439 jump to mind pretty quickly.
